learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to work, direct and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.

syllabus_topics: Automation of discrete event systems: basic concepts
Identification and marking of electrical automatisms
Identification and marking of pneumatic automatisms
Key concepts in continuous system control
Basic examples of continuous system control
Historical and market background of robotics. Current situation
Practice 0. Introduction (applicability of the subject using models)
Practice 1. Pneumatic Automatisms (analysis of pneumatic components)
Practice 2. Introduction to TIA PORTAL (first contact with Siemens TIA PORTAL environment for S7-1200 PLCs)
Practice 3. Programmed Automatisms 1 (basic automation exercise with GRAFCET, KOP, PLCs, and timers)
Practice 4. Programmed Automatisms 2 (medium difficulty exercise with TIA PORTAL, advanced control structures like simultaneous actions, exclusive actions, and end-of-cycle emergency stops)
Practice 5. Introduction to Matlab/Simulink (first contact with Matlab/Simulink environment)
Practice 6. Modeling and Identification of a dynamic system (applying laws to model plant dynamic behavior)
Practice 7. Design and tuning of a PID controller (tuning a predefined plant using trial and error and/or Ziegler-Nichols method)
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (including inverted classes and cooperative problem-solving)
Practical sessions (working in pairs, prior simulation tool work)
Expository classes in large groups (lectures, theory and general examples, introductory activities)
Small group classes (exercise resolution, practical activities, debates)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in in-person and/or virtual activities
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises

assessment_rules: To pass the course, both the theoretical exam and the practical work must be passed independently. A minimum score must be obtained in each of the course blocks, with the specific minimums detailed in the exam statements. Non-attendance to practical sessions automatically implies failing them.
